title: How 'Rocking in Rhythm' came about and Harry Carney's credit
summary: Bigard says Duke put Carney's name on 'Rocking in Rhythm' though Carney wrote nothing; the theme grew from his own humming and Braud and Carney joining behind two comedians in Baltimore, and Duke made the arrangement.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No. Well, now, Duke -- you see, Duke did a lot of things. Duke, he put Harry Carney's name on "Rocking in Rhythm. Harry Carney never wrote a thing in his life, you know. That's true. I'm not kidding.
You mean Harry didn't have a -- Why did Duke put his name on it?
I don't know. He never did. And you know how that was -- come about, "Rocking in Rhythm?"

We was playing the Pearl Theater in Baltimore -- not in -- yeah, Baltimore, and these two comedians, they had a little thing about the numbers. They didn't have no music but they used to just stand up there, the two by themselves, and say, "We -- I got the number." "Where did you get it from?" Just them two. And so I started out, I said, "C'mon, Johnny, let's get something together." So I started out (humming), and Johnny fell in. A little later on Braud started in. Then after Braud started in, then Harry Carney finally found a little part (humming), and made the third part. That's how that started.
Do you remember who the comedians were?
Yeah, Johnny Lee and another little short guy. I can't think of his name. And they had that little thing going.
How long after you started playing behind them did Duke start playing it with the band?
Duke made an arrangement on it.
